acceptance_criteria.criterion: Re-running when already registered is a no-op (idempotent).
--dry-run prints the JSON diff to stdout without writing any files.
VS Code user-level mcp.json contains a central_pm entry pointing to the shim path; no other keys are modified or reordered.
If mcp-server/dist/index.js does not exist, the script exits with a clear actionable error without writing any files.
The shim uses child_process.spawn with { stdio: 'inherit' } — stdout is not buffered at any point.
If ~/.ai-insights/config.json contains a path that no longer exists, the shim prints a diagnostic to stderr and exits with code 1.
A timestamped backup of the existing mcp.json is created before any merge write.
All paths use path.join() / os.homedir() — no hardcoded separators.

comments.note: Medium | A04 Insecure Design | scripts/install-mcp-global.js line 109-111 (shim _buildShimContent). The shim constructs distPath = join(repoPath, 'mcp-server', 'dist', 'index.js') and spawns it via Node.js without validating that distPath resolves within the configured repoPath boundary. A manually edited ~/.ai-insights/config.json pointing to an arbitrary .js file would cause that file to be executed in the MCP server context. Exploitability is LOW for this developer tool — config.json is in the user's home directory and writable only by the local user; an attacker with write access already has full user-level code execution. Remediation (defence-in-depth): add a path.resolve(distPath).startsWith(path.resolve(repoPath) + path.sep) containment check before spawn, and exit with a diagnostic if the check fails.

Info | A03 Injection — all spawnSync/spawn calls in installClaudeCode, uninstall, and the shim use shell: false (or the default, which is false) with argument arrays. No shell injection is possible. Process.execPath (Node.js binary) is used in the shim, not a user-controlled path — safe.

Info | A02 Cryptographic Failures — no cryptographic operations, no secrets, no credentials. config.json stores only a local filesystem path. VS Code mcp.json stores node executable + shim path. No data requiring encryption.
Info | A06 Vulnerable Components — no new npm dependencies introduced. Implementation uses only Node.js built-ins: fs, os, path, child_process. No CVE exposure.
